framework.name: next
framework.notes: App Router + React 19.2.8. next-intl plugin wrapped in next.config.mjs; root-level proxy.ts is a no-op passthrough (Next 16 replaced middleware.ts) so locales are cookie-based and URLs are NOT prefixed. output:'standalone' is applied only when process.env.VERCEL is unset. No turbopack key in next.config.mjs (Next 16 defaults).

monorepo.notes: single app; package.json has no workspaces field, no turbo/pnpm-workspace files. .github/nodejs.version pins 22; Dockerfile uses node:22-alpine.

auth.notes: better-auth 1.7.3. emailAndPassword always enabled; the Google social provider is registered only when GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID + GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET are both set (button separately gated by NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_AUTH_ENABLED). NO database adapter is passed to betterAuth() and no db/orm dependency exists anywhere, so session persistence is unverified. Role 'admin' comes from the AUTH_ADMIN_EMAILS CSV allowlist (or the demo accounts while NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO_MODE=true), otherwise 'user'. Permissions are dashboard.view:user / dashboard.view:admin; server guards requireUser()/requirePermission(); parallel-route slots @admin/@user both resolve to /dashboard, /profile, /settings.

observability: sentry (@sentry/nextjs, DSN-gated; next.config.mjs is NOT wrapped with withSentryConfig)

env.notes: Every var is .optional() with a fallback in src/libs/env.ts, so `next build` needs no environment at all (CI sets SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION=true; BETTER_AUTH_SECRET falls back to a 'PLEASE_SET_...' placeholder that only triggers a console.warn in production). .env.example documents only 4 of the 10 names (NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, BETTER_AUTH_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_AUTH_ENABLED, NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO_MODE). NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN is read directly in src/instrumentation-client.ts and appears in neither the env schema nor .env.example. The Docker build takes NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL / NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_AUTH_ENABLED / NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO_MODE as build ARGs. Only names were read; no values inspected.

deploy.notes: Multi-stage Dockerfile: node:22-alpine deps+builder -> gcr.io/distroless/nodejs22-debian12 runner (nonroot), copies .next/standalone + .next/static + public, EXPOSE 6767, HEALTHCHECK curls http://127.0.0.1:6767/api/health, CMD server.js (no shell). Port 6767 is hardcoded in scripts.dev/scripts.start and e2e/playwright.config.ts; only the standalone server honours the Dockerfile ENV PORT. docker-compose.yml builds the Dockerfile, maps 6767:6767 and loads .env via env_file. Vercel coupling: next.config.mjs drops standalone when VERCEL is set, better-auth trusts *.vercel.app, README ships a Deploy-to-Vercel button, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL points at the author deployment. No DB -> no migration step.

tests.notes: Unit/component tests are colocated as *.test.ts(x): button, card, demo/accounts, rbac/roles, schemas/login, schemas/register, libs/env, libs/utils, plus tests/auth/authorization.test.ts, tests/auth/roles.test.ts, tests/i18n/routing.test.ts (11 files). jsdom + @testing-library/react, shared renderWithProviders helper in tests/utils/render.tsx, config/vitest.config.ts forces SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION=true. E2E is one spec, e2e/home.spec.ts (home title, source-code link, /api/health json, /login field ids), with a self-started web server on 127.0.0.1:6767 - dev locally across chromium+firefox+webkit, production start:standalone + chromium only in CI. check.yml runs typecheck -> lint (oxlint + oxfmt) -> knip -> vitest -> build.

pitfalls.detail: Better Auth is wired with no persistence: betterAuth({...}) passes baseURL/secret/emailAndPassword/socialProviders but no `database`, and there is no db/orm dependency (no drizzle, prisma, sqlite, kysely) anywhere. The demo sign-in helper swallows sign-up errors (`catch { void error }`) and then signs in, so the credential panel looks functional while session storage is undefined.

README's project tree lists src/config/ (App navigation & feature flags) and public/llms.txt lists src/features/theme/, src/features/navigation/ and src/features/site/home-features.ts - none of these exist in the git tree; the real feature dirs are auth/, i18n/, site/.

README and llms.txt advertise AUTH_ADMIN_EMAILS *or* NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_ADMIN_EMAILS for admin access, but src/libs/env.ts only defines the server-side AUTH_ADMIN_EMAILS; the NEXT_PUBLIC_ variant is never read. README also says 'TypeScript 6' while package.json pins typescript 7.0.2.

README claims 'Every variable is documented in .env.example' and 'Set environment variables from .env.example in Vercel project settings', but .env.example contains only 4 of the 10 names the code reads (missing BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, AUTH_ADMIN_EMAILS, SENTRY_DSN, NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN).

Sentry is installed and initialised but next.config.mjs is not wrapped with withSentryConfig and neither DSN name appears in .env.example, so error tracking silently no-ops; even with a DSN no source maps would be uploaded.

/unauthorized sits inside the (protected) route group whose layout calls requireUser(), so an unauthenticated visitor is redirected to /login and never reaches the unauthorized page; it is only reachable while signed in with the wrong role. The (auth) layout mirrors this by bouncing signed-in users to /dashboard.
`prepare` runs `lefthook install || true` on every npm install, so a fresh checkout writes .git/hooks (needs a git repo with a writable .git; harmless in a bare tarball because of the || true).

sharp is overridden to ^0.35.4 and whitelisted in package.json allowScripts, so its install script must run to fetch the native binary; installing with --ignore-scripts leaves next/image on a degraded optimizer. The same allowScripts block gates @sentry/cli, @swc/core and @parcel/watcher.

Dependency graph is advanced/future-pinned: next 16.3.4 + react 19.2.8 + typescript 7.0.2 + tailwind 4.3.3, several @radix-ui packages pinned to exact versions, and 5 overrides (kysely, postcss, sharp, uuid, @swc/helpers). Reproduce with `npm ci` as the Dockerfile and CI do; a lockfile-free install can drift into conflicting majors.

README headlines '50+ custom & reusable UI components' and shows a Lighthouse screenshot, but the repo ships 44 files under src/components/ui (42 components, 2 of them tests) and the Lighthouse image is a static public/*.webp - no performance evidence is reproducible from the code.

verdict.best_for: A frontend-first Next.js 16 SaaS/admin shell where the backend already exists: auth pages, RBAC role slots, sidebar dashboards, 42 UI primitives and a 6-locale RTL-aware i18n layer are done and ready to point at your own REST/GraphQL API.
verdict.weak_for: Anything that must store data itself - there is no database, ORM, migrations, billing, email, uploads, jobs or search code, and Better Auth has no adapter wired, so accounts and sessions must be finished before the demo credentials mean anything.
verdict.swap_burden: light - nothing paid is load-bearing (Sentry and Vercel Analytics are DSN-gated and deletable) and branding/SEO is centralised in src/features/site/site.config.json plus messages/
